notes:
Union Council of Ministers as of 2026-09-25 (Third Modi ministry, formed 9-10 June 2024).

METHOD: Base roster reconstructed from the live Wikipedia "Third Modi ministry" article
(en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third_Modi_ministry, fetched via the Wikipedia parse API on 2026-09-25), which
lists 30 Cabinet Ministers, 5 Ministers of State (Independent Charge) and 34 Ministers of State
(72 total members ever appointed, 3 removed by 2026-09-25, 69 currently serving). Per-holder house
(Lok Sabha/Rajya Sabha), constituency and party were extracted from each holder's own Wikipedia
infobox (fetched individually) and cross-checked with WebSearch news coverage for every change
event below. One position per (ministry, seat): a minister holding N ministries gets N
`in-pos-minister-<slug>` / `in-pos-mos-<slug>-<n>` records, holder repeated, cross-referenced in notes.

CHANGES SINCE JUNE 2024 (verified against 2026 press coverage, not just Wikipedia):
1. Education: Dharmendra Pradhan resigned as Union Education Minister on 25 July 2026 following
   weeks of nationwide student protests over an examination-leak scandal (President accepted his
   resignation under Article 75). Pralhad Joshi (already Cabinet Minister for Consumer Affairs,
   Food & Public Distribution and New & Renewable Energy) was given additional charge of Education
   the same day. Sources: SCC Online, Al Jazeera (2026-07-25/26).
2. George Kurian (MoS Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying; MoS Minority Affairs) left the
   Council of Ministers on 23 June 2026 after his Rajya Sabha term ended 21 June 2026 and BJP did
   not renominate him. No replacement had been named for either portfolio as of 2026-09-25
   (in-pos-mos-fisheries-animal-husbandry-and-dairying-2 and in-pos-mos-minority-affairs-1 are
   recorded vacant, confidence "low" pending a reshuffle). Source: The Tribune, Business Standard.
3. Ravneet Singh Bittu (MoS Railways; MoS Food Processing Industries) resigned 24 July 2026 after
   similarly not being renominated to the Rajya Sabha (his term ended 21 June 2026); reported bound
   for a party role ahead of the 2027 Punjab election. No replacement named as of 2026-09-25
   (in-pos-mos-railways-2 and in-pos-mos-food-processing-industries-1 recorded vacant, confidence
   "low"). Source: Newsdrum, Tribune India.

RESHUFFLE WATCH (not applied — no confirmed action as of 2026-09-25): Speculation about a larger Modi
Cabinet reshuffle/expansion has recurred through mid-2026 (expected around a "Chintan Shivir"
ministers' retreat PM Modi held 23-24 September 2026), including talk of Nirmala Sitharaman moving
portfolios and new inductees (Shaktikanta Das, Anurag Thakur, Shrikant Shinde, Arun Govil were
named in speculation). As of 2026-09-25 the government has made no official announcement and no new
minister has been sworn in beyond the changes listed above — do not treat the speculation as fact;
re-check this segment after any confirmed swearing-in.

DATA GAPS / LOW CONFIDENCE:
- Tokhan Sahu (MoS Housing & Urban Affairs): his Wikipedia infobox heading just says "Member of
  Parliament" without naming the house; house inferred as Lok Sabha from his constituency
  (Bilaspur, Chhattisgarh, a Lok Sabha seat) — confidence "medium" on that position pending a
  direct-source check.
- MoS Finance shows only one holder (Pankaj Chaudhary) in the current Wikipedia table; if a second
  MoS Finance exists it was not surfaced by this pass.
- `since` dates for all June-2024 appointees use the Wikipedia-listed "took office" date (10 June
  2024 for most; 9 June 2024 for the PM), not each individual's personal swearing-in time.
- No PIB "allocation of portfolios" gazette notification was fetched directly (network access here
  was via WebSearch/WebFetch + the Wikipedia API, not gov.in scraping); all current-holder facts
  are corroborated by at least one 2026 press source in addition to Wikipedia, per the quality bar,
  but a direct PIB citation was not obtained for every seat.
